# jgengine-ui — exported API surface

## @jgengine/core/dialog/dialogBehavior.view

- `DialogBehaviorOptions` (interface): interface DialogBehaviorOptions — Options for controlled dialog focus behavior; callers own markup, state, and close policy.
- `useDialogBehavior` (function): function useDialogBehavior<T extends HTMLElement = HTMLDivElement>(options: DialogBehaviorOptions): RefObject<T | null> — Focus entry, Tab trapping, Escape requests, and focus restoration for a caller-owned dialog. Attach the returned ref to the dialog root and supply `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, an accessible name, and `tabIndex={-1}`. The most recently opened dialog handles keys, including portal roots. Closing an inner dialog restores its opener; cleanup never steals focus from another active dialog. Replacing the root while open keeps its position and original return target.

## @jgengine/core/dialog/modalStack

- `MODAL_CANCEL` (const): const MODAL_CANCEL: "cancel" — Conventional cancel/dismiss result (also the default auto-dismiss and pop result).
- `MODAL_CONFIRM` (const): const MODAL_CONFIRM: "confirm" — Conventional confirm result for a two-button dialog — a shared string, not model behavior.
- `ModalInput` (type): type ModalInput = Omit<ModalRecord, "id"> & { id?: string } — A modal to push — {@link ModalRecord} with an optional id (auto-assigned when absent).
- `ModalRecord` (interface): interface ModalRecord — Headless, serializable model for a stack of modal dialogs — the data layer behind a pause menu, a "quit to menu?" confirmation, a level-up popup, or any blocking overlay a game raises over its scene. It carries an ordered stack of opaque {@link ModalRecord}s (push to open, pop/resolve to close) and nothing about how they look: the model NEVER interprets a record's `kind` or a resolution's `result` string — those are free-form game vocabulary the React chrome in `@jgengine/react` renders. Observable ({@link ModalStack.subscribe}) and round-trips through a save ({@link ModalStack.snapshot}/{@link ModalStack.restore}). An injected clock powers optional per-modal auto-dismiss timers; leave those unset and the model is pure and clockless.
- `ModalResolution` (interface): interface ModalResolution — The outcome of closing a modal via {@link ModalStack.resolve} (or an auto-dismiss) — the closed record's identity plus the free-form `result` string the caller chose. Delivered to the `onResolve` option and stashed as {@link ModalStack.lastResolution}.
- `ModalStack` (interface): interface ModalStack — An observable, serializable stack of modal dialogs. See {@link createModalStack}.
- `ModalStackEntry` (interface): interface ModalStackEntry — A serialized stack entry: the opaque record plus the clock time it opened (for timer restore).
- `ModalStackOptions` (interface): interface ModalStackOptions — Options for {@link createModalStack}.
- `ModalStackSnapshot` (interface): interface ModalStackSnapshot — Serializable state — the ordered entries (bottom-first) and the id counter. Plain JSON.
- `createModalStack` (function): function createModalStack(options: ModalStackOptions = {}): ModalStack — A stack of modal dialogs: push opaque records to open blocking overlays (a pause menu, a confirm prompt, a reward popup), pop or resolve them with a free-form result to close, and query the top / open / depth to gate game input. The model is deliberately vocabulary-free — it never reads a record's `kind` or a resolution's `result`, so a game owns every dialog style — and fully serializable, with an optional injected clock driving per-modal auto-dismiss. A React host renders `top()`; `subscribe` re-renders it, `snapshot`/`restore` round-trip it through a save.

## @jgengine/core/dialog/modals.view

- `ConfirmDialog` (function): function ConfirmDialog({ title, body, confirmLabel = "Confirm", cancelLabel = "Cancel", onConfirm, onCancel, danger = false, width = 360, className, style, }: ConfirmDialogProps): ReactNode — A generic two-button confirmation dialog — title, optional body, and Cancel / Confirm buttons over a `HudTheme`-token-driven {@link HudSurface}. Presentation-only: wire `onConfirm`/`onCancel` to a modal stack's `resolve` (typically inside a {@link ModalHost} render callback) and reskin via `HudTheme` tokens or `danger` for a destructive action. It interprets nothing — the game supplies the copy.
- `ConfirmDialogProps` (interface): interface ConfirmDialogProps — Props for {@link ConfirmDialog}.
- `ModalControls` (interface): interface ModalControls — Stack-bound controls handed to a {@link ModalHost} render callback.
- `ModalHost` (function): function ModalHost({ stack, children, showBackdrop = true, backdrop, closeOnBackdrop = true, closeOnEsc = true, zIndexBase = 80, onInteract, className, style, }: ModalHostProps): ReactNode — Full-screen modal host: watches a stack, renders only the topmost modal centered over a dimmed backdrop, and manages accessibility — the panel is a `role="dialog" aria-modal`, focus moves into it on open and is trapped with Tab/Shift+Tab cycling, Escape and (optionally) a backdrop click cancel the top modal, and focus returns to the previously focused element on close. It renders nothing when the stack is empty. Skin the panel and backdrop via `HudTheme` tokens.
- `ModalHostProps` (interface): interface ModalHostProps — Props for {@link ModalHost}.
- `ModalStackView` (interface): interface ModalStackView — React chrome over the headless modal stack (`@jgengine/core/dialog/modalStack`) — the blocking-overlay layer a game raises over its scene: a pause menu, a "quit to menu?" confirm, a reward popup. {@link useModalStack} is the DATA/HOOK layer (subscribe + the active record), {@link ModalHost} renders the top modal with a backdrop, focus trap, and Esc-to-cancel, and {@link ConfirmDialog} / {@link PauseMenu} (`menu/pauseMenu`) are ready-to-wire, HudTheme-token-driven building blocks. All unskinned and game-owned: the model never interprets a modal's `kind`, so a game switches on it to pick which of these (or its own) content to show, and reskins everything via `HudTheme` tokens and the frame.
- `useModalStack` (function): function useModalStack(stack: ModalStack): ModalStackView — Subscribe to a modal stack and re-render on every change, returning the active modal and depth.

## @jgengine/core/hud/comboMeter.view

- `ComboMeterHud` (function): function ComboMeterHud({ meter, tierColors, theme, animate = true, hideWhenEmpty = true, barWidth = 220, className, style, }: ComboMeterHudProps): ReactNode — A drop-in HUD for a core {@link ComboMeter}: the big live combo count ("×12"), the current free-string tier label, the derived score multiplier, and a draining window bar (reusing the shared atomic bar) that empties as the decay window runs out and re-fills on every hit. The active tier's color — supplied by the game via `tierColors`, keyed on the free-string tier id the model never interprets — drives the count glow, the label, and the bar fill, so a game reskins the escalation ("good" → "great" → "savage") without the engine hardcoding any tier meaning. Presentation only: all counting, timing, tiers, and the multiplier live in the core model.
- `ComboMeterHudProps` (interface): interface ComboMeterHudProps — Props for {@link ComboMeterHud}.
- `ComboMeterTheme` (interface): interface ComboMeterTheme — Reskin tokens for {@link ComboMeterHud}.
- `useComboMeter` (function): function useComboMeter(meter: ComboMeter, animate = true): ComboMeterView — Subscribe to a combo meter and re-render it each animation frame so the decay window bar drains live, returning the pooled view to draw right now. Reading the view each frame advances the meter's clock and fires window expiry, so a combo that times out visibly drops even with no further hits. The returned object is the model's pooled view — read its fields immediately, do not retain it.

The game keeps owning its entities: it passes a plain array of `{ id, worldPosition }` entries and a `project` function that turns a world position into a screen point, and composes each frame's markup itself (typically a `KitMeter` plus a name) drawn by the active UI kit. Stable for equal depths via `id`. No React, no DOM — unit-testable in isolation.

## @jgengine/core/hud/floatingText

- `FloatingTextDef` (interface): interface FloatingTextDef — One text pop to spawn: what to say, where in the world, and how it moves and fades. Everything but `position` and `text` is optional and falls back to the field's defaults. `kind` is a free-form tag (`"damage"`, `"heal"`, `"crit"`, `"xp"`, `"gold"`, `"bark"`, …) the presentation layer styles — the model never interprets it, so nothing here is combat- or genre-specific.
- `FloatingTextField` (interface): interface FloatingTextField — A live, dt-driven field of world-anchored floating text.
- `FloatingTextFieldConfig` (interface): interface FloatingTextFieldConfig — Construction options for {@link createFloatingTextField}.
- `FloatingTextPosition` (type): type FloatingTextPosition = readonly [number, number, number] — A world-space anchor `[x, y, z]` a floating-text entry rises from.
- `FloatingTextSnapshot` (interface): interface FloatingTextSnapshot — Serializable state for save/restore and deterministic replay.
- `FloatingTextView` (interface): interface FloatingTextView — A live entry resolved for rendering: current world position and fade/scale over life.
- `createFloatingTextField` (function): function createFloatingTextField(config: FloatingTextFieldConfig = {}): FloatingTextField — A generic, allocation-aware field of world-anchored floating text: damage numbers, heals, crits, XP/gold gains, status pops, dialogue barks — anything a game wants to say at a point in the world for a moment. It is dt-driven (call `update(dt)` each frame) and deterministic: the only randomness is the horizontal drift jitter, which flows from the injected `seed`, so the same seed and the same emit/update sequence reproduce identical motion, and `snapshot`/`restore` round-trips the live pool. The model owns only the spawn → rise/drift → fade → reap lifecycle: `kind` is a free string and `color` a passthrough hint, so nothing here couples to combat or any genre. Presentation (projecting each entry to the screen and styling it per `kind`) lives in `@jgengine/react`'s `FloatingText`.

## @jgengine/core/hud/hudLayout.view

Each `HudPanel` names an anchor and a priority; the canvas measures every panel and places them all at once so none lands on another, at any screen size. Panels sharing an anchor stack outward from that edge; a panel that would cover a neighbour slides along its edge to the nearest free spot; when the screen is too small, the lowest-priority panels fold into a toggle, and only then does the whole HUD shrink. Device safe areas and every touch control (any region registered as kind `control` or `system`) are kept clear. Games declare panels, never place them per size.

## @jgengine/core/hud/hudPanelLayout

- `HudPanelClaim` (interface): interface HudPanelClaim — One HUD panel asking for room. Panels that share an `anchor` stack outward from that edge in `order`; the solver then moves, collapses or shrinks whatever would land on something else.
- `HudPanelLayout` (interface): interface HudPanelLayout — Where every panel landed.
- `HudPanelLayoutRequest` (interface): interface HudPanelLayoutRequest — The screen the panels share.
- `arrangeHudPanels` (function): function arrangeHudPanels(claims: readonly HudPanelClaim[], request: HudPanelLayoutRequest): HudPanelLayout — Lay out every HUD panel on one screen without overlap. Panels start stacked at their anchors; a panel that would land on another slides along its edge or down its stack to the nearest free spot. When no spot is free, the lowest-priority panel folds into its toggle, and when even that is not enough the whole HUD shrinks a step at a time down to `minScale`. A panel that only fits by leaving its edge for the middle of the screen (a bottom bar lifted over the play view by a touch dock) also shrinks the HUD, and stays lifted only when no zoom down to `minScale` keeps it on its edge. Higher priority places first, then declaration order. Pure: the same claims on the same screen give the same layout.

The canvas stacks each corner, slides what does not fit beside it, and folds the lowest priority into a toggle on a small screen. Screenshots at any viewport without a block landing on a neighbour.

A pair is skipped when either side's policy is `allow`, when either opts into the other via `allowOverlapWith`, when they share a `collisionGroup`, or when the overlap is below `minArea`.

- `HudFitConfig` (interface): interface HudFitConfig — Design-resolution fit for the HUD surface. ## @jgengine/core/i18n/i18n

- `Catalog` (type): type Catalog = Readonly<Record<Locale, Messages>> — All locales' message tables, keyed by locale.
- `I18n` (interface): interface I18n — Runtime translator over a message {@link Catalog} — active locale, lookup with fallback, interpolation, and pluralization.
- `I18nOptions` (interface): interface I18nOptions — Configuration for {@link createI18n}.
- `Locale` (type): type Locale = string — A locale tag (e.g. `"en"`, `"es"`, `"ja"`) — a key into a {@link Catalog}.
- `Messages` (type): type Messages = Readonly<Record<string, string>> — Flat message table for one locale: key → template string with `{param}` slots.
- `TParams` (type): type TParams = Readonly<Record<string, string | number>> — Interpolation values for a message template.
- `createI18n` (function): function createI18n(options: I18nOptions): I18n — Create a translator over a message catalog: active-locale lookup with a fallback-locale chain, `{param}` interpolation, and `Intl.PluralRules`-based pluralization. Observable (`subscribe`) so React re-renders on `setLocale`; the catalog is caller-owned static data, the locale is the only state.
- `interpolate` (function): function interpolate(template: string, params?: TParams): string — Replace `{name}` placeholders in `template` with `params[name]`. Unknown placeholders are left intact. Pure and locale-independent.

- `useT` (function): function useT(): (key: string, params?: TParams) => string — Return the translator bound to the current locale; the component re-renders when `setLocale` is called, so returned strings stay live.

## @jgengine/core/menu/menuNav

- `MENU_KEY_INTENTS` (const): const MENU_KEY_INTENTS: Readonly<Record<string, MenuIntent>> — Keyboard codes that drive a menu, by `KeyboardEvent.code`. Tab is deliberately absent: it stays native.
- `MenuIntent` (type): type MenuIntent = MenuNavDirection | "confirm" | "back" — Everything a key or gamepad button can ask a menu to do.
- `MenuNavDirection` (type): type MenuNavDirection = "up" | "down" | "left" | "right" | "first" | "last" — Headless focus-order model for a game front-end menu: a list or grid of item ids, one focused item, and the keyboard/gamepad intents that move between them. It holds no React state, no DOM and no look — `@jgengine/core/menu/menuNav.view` binds it to a container and real focus, and each game decides what the items are and where they sit.
- `MenuNavHold` (interface): interface MenuNavHold — When a held direction was pressed and when it last moved the focus.
- `MenuNavLayout` (interface): interface MenuNavLayout — The shape of the item list being navigated: how many items, how they wrap into rows.
- `MenuNavRepeat` (interface): interface MenuNavRepeat — Hold-to-repeat timing for a held d-pad/stick: one immediate move, then repeats.
- `menuIntentForKey` (function): function menuIntentForKey(code: string): MenuIntent | null — Resolve a `KeyboardEvent.code` to a menu intent, or `null` for keys the menu leaves alone (typing, Tab, shortcuts). Escape and Backspace both mean back; Space and Enter both mean confirm.
- `menuIntentForPadAxis` (function): function menuIntentForPadAxis(axis: number, value: number, deadzone = 0.55): MenuNavDirection | null — Resolve a left-stick axis sample to a direction. Axis `0` is horizontal and axis `1` vertical (standard mapping, up is negative); the larger magnitude wins so a diagonal push is one move.
- `menuIntentForPadButton` (function): function menuIntentForPadButton(button: number): MenuIntent | null — Standard-mapping gamepad buttons as menu intents: A/Cross confirms, B/Circle and Start back, the d-pad moves. Buttons with no menu meaning return `null`.
- `menuNavIdAt` (function): function menuNavIdAt(ids: readonly string[], index: number): string | null — The id at `index`, or `null` outside the list.
- `menuNavIndex` (function): function menuNavIndex(ids: readonly string[], id: string | null | undefined): number — The index of `id` in the focus order, or `-1` when it is not part of this menu.
- `menuNavMove` (function): function menuNavMove(index: number, direction: MenuNavDirection, layout: MenuNavLayout): number — The next focused index for a direction, or the same index when the move is a no-op. Moves skip `disabled` indices and stop (rather than wrap) when every item in the way is disabled, so a menu can never hand focus to a dead row.
- `shouldRepeatMenuNav` (function): function shouldRepeatMenuNav(now: number, hold: MenuNavHold, repeat: MenuNavRepeat = {}): boolean — Whether a held direction should fire a move at `now`: immediately on press, then only after `delayMs`, and no more often than `intervalMs`. Pure timing, so a gamepad poll and a keydown handler share one rule.

## @jgengine/core/menu/menuNav.view

- `MenuNavContainerProps` (interface): interface MenuNavContainerProps — The container props that make a menu navigable.
- `MenuNavController` (interface): interface MenuNavController — The live navigation controller returned by {@link useMenuNav}.
- `MenuNavItemProps` (interface): interface MenuNavItemProps — Props a menu item needs so {@link useMenuNav} can focus it and track pointer/focus.
- `MenuNavRender` (type): type MenuNavRender = (nav: MenuNavController) => ReactNode — Render prop for a menu whose items come from {@link useMenuNav}.
- `UseMenuNavOptions` (interface): interface UseMenuNavOptions — How {@link useMenuNav} is wired.
- `useMenuNav` (function): function useMenuNav({ ids, columns = 1, wrap = true, disabled, initialId, enabled = true, onConfirm, onBack, onAdjust, gamepad = true, repeat, }: UseMenuNavOptions): MenuNavController — Bind a menu's focus order to the DOM: arrow keys, WASD, Home/End and a standard gamepad move a roving focus, Enter/Space/A confirm, Escape/Backspace/B/Start go back. Tab is left to the browser, so a menu never traps focus, and typing in a text field is never intercepted. The menu is pure state + listeners — it unmounts with the screen, so it costs nothing during play.

## @jgengine/core/menu/menuRouter.view

- `MenuRouter` (interface): interface MenuRouter<Id extends string> — A menu screen stack: where you are, how you got there, and how to go back.
- `MenuStackAction` (type): type MenuStackAction<Id extends string> = | { type: "open"; id: Id } | { type: "back" } | { type: "replace"; id: Id } | { type: "reset"; id?: Id } — A screen-stack transition. `reset` without an id collapses to the router's original root.
- `menuStackReducer` (function): function menuStackReducer<Id extends string>(path: readonly Id[], action: MenuStackAction<Id>, root: Id): readonly Id[] — The pure screen-stack transition behind {@link useMenuRouter}. Exported so a game can drive the same navigation from its own store or a replayable command log instead of React state.
- `useMenuRouter` (function): function useMenuRouter<Id extends string>(root: Id, options: { escapeToBack?: boolean } = {}): MenuRouter<Id> — The screen stack behind a game front-end: title → save select → settings → credits, and Escape back out. Every game menu needs this and none of it is game-specific, so it ships here rather than being re-derived per game. Holds no content and imposes no look — the game decides what each screen id renders.

## @jgengine/core/menu/menuScreen.view

- `MenuScreen` (function): function MenuScreen({ open = true, transition = "fade", scrim = "dim", coversCanvas = false, enterMs = 220, exitMs = 160, reducedMotion, label, role = "dialog", backdrop, className, style, contentClassName, contentStyle, children, onClosed, }: MenuScreenProps): ReactNode — One animated screen of a game front-end: full-bleed, laid out by the game, with an enter/exit animation that runs on transform/opacity only (no layout, no frame hitch) and unmounts when the exit finishes. The scrim is translucent and the optional `backdrop` slot paints behind the content, so a live 3D scene stays visible behind a title, pause or settings screen. Durations come from the caller or collapse to zero under reduced motion.
- `MenuScreenProps` (interface): interface MenuScreenProps — Props for {@link MenuScreen}.
- `MenuScreenScrim` (type): type MenuScreenScrim = "none" | "dim" | "blur" — How much a {@link MenuScreen} dims the scene behind it. `none` keeps a live 3D scene fully visible.
- `MenuScreenTransition` (type): type MenuScreenTransition = "fade" | "slide" | "scale" | "none" — Which motion a {@link MenuScreen} uses when it enters and leaves.

## @jgengine/core/menu/menuTransition

- `MenuTransition` (interface): interface MenuTransition — Observable enter/exit phase machine.
- `MenuTransitionConfig` (interface): interface MenuTransitionConfig — Durations and accessibility policy for one transition.
- `MenuTransitionPhase` (type): type MenuTransitionPhase = "closed" | "enter" | "open" | "exit" — The phase timing behind an animated menu screen: closed → entering → open → exiting → closed. Pure timing over an injected clock, so a React block can animate with CSS and still know exactly when an exit finished and the screen may unmount. Reduced motion collapses every duration to zero instead of skipping the state machine, so callers never branch on it.
- `MenuTransitionSnapshot` (interface): interface MenuTransitionSnapshot — Serializable phase state.
- `createMenuTransition` (function): function createMenuTransition(config: MenuTransitionConfig = {}, initial?: MenuTransitionSnapshot): MenuTransition — Create a {@link MenuTransition}. `open`/`close` start a phase; `tick` advances it once its duration has elapsed. Nothing schedules timers here — the caller ticks from its animation loop or a timeout.
- `menuTransitionDurations` (function): function menuTransitionDurations(config: MenuTransitionConfig = {}): { enter: number; exit: number } — The enter and exit durations after reduced-motion is applied.
- `menuTransitionPhaseMs` (function): function menuTransitionPhaseMs(phase: MenuTransitionPhase, config: MenuTransitionConfig = {}): number — How long the current phase lasts, in ms (0 for open/closed).

The game fills the verbs (Resume, Save, Settings, Quit) and the detail pane, and reskins it with `--jg-*` tokens on `style`. Escape (or B/Start) resumes.
- `PauseMenuProps` (type): type PauseMenuProps = Omit<GameMenuProps, "variant"> & { /** Resume play. Escape, B and Start call it too unless `onBack` is given. */ onResume?: () => void; } — Props for {@link PauseMenu}: every {@link GameMenu} knob except `variant`, plus `onResume`.

- `QuickMenu` (function): function QuickMenu({ items, layout = "list", onSelect, onClose, title, columns = 3, arc = { startAngle: Math.PI / 2, sweep: Math.PI }, radialSize = 300, accent = "var(--jg-accent, #38bdf8)", className, style, }: QuickMenuProps): ReactNode — Versatile quick menu that takes many forms — a `radial` wheel, a partial `arc`, a vertical `list`, or a `grid` — over one item model with icons, labels, hotkeys, count badges, cooldowns, section headers, and nested submenus (drill in / back). Radial and arc forms reuse {@link RadialMenu}; list and grid render sectioned rows/tiles. The game supplies content and skin.

## @jgengine/core/menu/radialMenu

- `RadialArc` (interface): interface RadialArc — Arc the slices span. Omit for a full wheel (index 0 at the top). A partial `sweep` (e.g. `Math.PI` for a bottom half, `Math.PI / 2` for a quarter) packs the slices evenly inside `[startAngle, startAngle + sweep]` — the arc/quick-bar forms. Angles are radians from "up" (−Y), clockwise.
- `RadialSlice` (interface): interface RadialSlice — One wedge of a radial menu — geometry for rendering a slice. Angles are radians from "up" (−Y), clockwise.
- `RadialVectorOptions` (interface): interface RadialVectorOptions extends RadialArc — Options for {@link radialIndexFromVector}.
- `radialIndexFromAngle` (function): function radialIndexFromAngle(angle: number, count: number, arc?: RadialArc): number — Map an angle to a slice index; returns -1 when the angle falls outside a partial `arc`.
- `radialIndexFromVector` (function): function radialIndexFromVector(dx: number, dy: number, count: number, options: RadialVectorOptions = {}): number | null — Pick the slice a pointer/stick vector points at. `dx`/`dy` are screen-space (y down): up is `(0, -1)`. Returns null inside `deadZone` or (for a partial `arc`) outside the arc, so a centered stick or a click off the arc selects nothing.
- `radialSlicePosition` (function): function radialSlicePosition(index: number, count: number, radius: number, arc?: RadialArc): { x: number; y: number } — Unit-circle position of a slice center (up = `(0, -1)`), scaled by `radius` — where to place a wedge's icon/label.
- `radialSlices` (function): function radialSlices(count: number, arc?: RadialArc): RadialSlice[] — Divide a ring (or `arc`) into `count` wedges — the geometry a radial/quick menu (weapon wheel, emote arc, ping bar) renders. A full wheel centers index 0 at the top; a partial `arc` packs the slices inside its sweep.

## @jgengine/core/menu/radialMenu.view

- `RadialMenu` (function): function RadialMenu({ options, open = true, onSelect, onClose, size = 300, innerRadius = 52, arc, highlightIndex, accent = "var(--jg-accent, #38bdf8)", className, style, }: RadialMenuProps): ReactNode — Radial / quick menu (weapon or emote wheel) — a ring or partial `arc` of selectable wedges the player points at with the mouse (or a stick). Pointer angle drives the highlight via core `radialIndexFromVector`; click/confirm fires `onSelect`, the neutral hub closes. Options carry optional hotkeys, count badges, cooldowns, and submenu markers. The game supplies icons/labels and skins it.
- `RadialMenuOption` (interface): interface RadialMenuOption — One selectable entry on a radial/quick menu (weapon or emote wheel).
- `RadialMenuProps` (interface): interface RadialMenuProps — Props for {@link RadialMenu}.

## @jgengine/core/menu/startScreen.view

- `ControlHint` (interface): interface ControlHint — One row of a control legend. Name the game action(s) whose bound key(s) to show (`action`) so the glyphs come straight from the keybind map — never re-typed — or give literal `keys` for controls that live outside the map (`"Mouse"`, `"LMB"`). `label` says what the control does.
- `ControlsList` (function): function ControlsList({ bindings, controls, hideOnCoarsePointer = true, separator = " / ", className, rowClassName, keysClassName, keyClassName, separatorClassName, labelClassName, renderKey, renderRow, }: { bindings?: ActionCodesMap; controls: readonly ControlHint[]; hideOnCoarsePointer?: boolean; … — Renders a controls legend whose key glyphs come from the game's keybind map, so bindings live in one place and never drift from a hand-typed table. Hides itself on coarse-pointer devices (a touchscreen has no keyboard) via the same `data-jg-kbd-hint` marker as `KeyHint`. Headless: every part carries a `className` slot and `data-*` hook; pass `renderKey`/`renderRow` to fully own the markup.
- `StartScreen` (function): function StartScreen({ open = true, className, style, children, settings, settingsPlacement = "top-right", settingsClassName, settingsWrapperClassName, }: { open?: boolean; className?: string; style?: CSSProperties; children?: ReactNode; settings?: boolean | ReactNode; settingsPlacement?: StartScree… — Composable title/attract-screen scaffold: a full-bleed `data-jg-menu` overlay that positions and centers the game's own content, with an opt-in settings corner. It imposes no look — the game supplies the title, art, and buttons as children and styles the container through `className`/`style` (per the composable-chrome rule: a placement hook, not a mandated menu).
- `StartScreenCorner` (type): type StartScreenCorner = "top-left" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-right" — Which corner of a `StartScreen` the opt-in settings slot is pinned to.

## @jgengine/core/play/playRunner.draw

- `PlayRunOptions` (interface): interface PlayRunOptions — Options for one scripted play run.
- `runPlayScript` (function): function runPlayScript(playable: PlayableGame, spec: PlayScript | PlayScriptSpec, options: PlayRunOptions = {}): PlayRunResult — Play a real game without a browser: boot its `PlayableGame` through the headless runner, apply a tick-based {@link PlayScript}, and return what happened plus whether the script's assertions held.

## @jgengine/core/play/script

- `PLAY_MOVE_ACTIONS` (const): const PLAY_MOVE_ACTIONS: Readonly<Record<PlayMove, string>> — Movement action ids a {@link PlayMove} holds, so a script walks through the same controller a player does.
- `PlayAimStep` (interface): interface PlayAimStep extends PlayStepBase — Point the walk controller and the aim payload at a yaw/pitch, in radians.
- `PlayCommandStep` (interface): interface PlayCommandStep extends PlayStepBase — Run a registered command directly, with whatever input it declares.
- `PlayExpectation` (interface): interface PlayExpectation — One assertion about world state. Read happens twice — right after `setup` and on the assertion's own tick — so a script can prove change ("health dropped") as well as a level ("wave is 2").
- `PlayFireStep` (interface): interface PlayFireStep extends PlayStepBase — Hold the `fire` action: the bound `fire` command runs on the press tick, then on its repeat cadence.
- `PlayMove` (type): type PlayMove = "forward" | "back" | "left" | "right" — Direction a scripted step walks, using the shell's own movement actions.
- `PlayMoveStep` (interface): interface PlayMoveStep extends PlayStepBase — Hold a movement direction for `ticks` — the shell walk controller's own held actions.
- `PlayScript` (interface): interface PlayScript — A script to play against a real game: what to do, on which tick, and what must be true afterwards.
- `PlayScriptSpec` (interface): interface PlayScriptSpec — What {@link createPlayScript} accepts: the same script with the derived fields optional.
- `PlayStep` (type): type PlayStep = PlayMoveStep | PlayAimStep | PlayFireStep | PlayUseStep | PlayWaitStep | PlayCommandStep — One tick-based action in a script.
- `PlayUseStep` (interface): interface PlayUseStep extends PlayStepBase — Press one bound action id once (default one tick) — `interact`, `reload`, `useAbility`, a game's own action.
- `PlayValue` (type): type PlayValue = number | string | boolean | null — A reading an assertion compares: a stat, a distance, a count, a phase id.
- `PlayWaitStep` (interface): interface PlayWaitStep extends PlayStepBase — Hold nothing for `ticks`, letting the world run.
- `createPlayScript` (function): function createPlayScript(spec: PlayScriptSpec): PlayScript — Validate and normalize a script: whole-tick timings, sorted steps, a derived run length.

## @jgengine/core/play/timeline

- `PlayExpectationResult` (interface): interface PlayExpectationResult — One assertion's verdict, with both readings so a failure says what changed and by how much.
- `PlayRunResult` (interface): interface PlayRunResult — Everything a scripted run produced: the timeline, the assertion verdicts, and a digest of the timeline for replay comparison.
- `PlayTimelineEntry` (interface): interface PlayTimelineEntry — One row of what happened, on the tick it happened.
- `PlayTimelineKind` (type): type PlayTimelineKind = "step" | "command" | "event" | "check" — What a timeline row records: a scripted action, a command result, a world event, or an assertion reading.
- `formatPlayTimelineEntry` (function): function formatPlayTimelineEntry(entry: PlayTimelineEntry): string — One compact timeline line: `t=120 event combat.damage to=bruiser amount=12 remaining=54`.
- `playTimelineDigest` (function): function playTimelineDigest(timeline: readonly PlayTimelineEntry[]): string — FNV-1a over the timeline's canonical JSON. Cheap, dependency-free and stable across runs and machines, which is all a replay comparison needs.

## @jgengine/core/render/ambientLife

- `AmbientLifeConfig` (interface): interface AmbientLifeConfig — Small life the renderer adds around the camera, driven by the weather and the time of day. Birds circle overhead in fair daylight and leave in rain or at night; litter blows along the ground when the wind picks up; steam rises from vents, thicker when it is cold, wet or dark.
- `SteamVent` (interface): interface SteamVent — A point that breathes steam: a manhole, a vent, a hot spring, a kettle on a stall.

## @jgengine/core/render/colorPipeline

- `AutoExposureConfig` (interface): interface AutoExposureConfig — Bounds and adaptation policy for clamped auto-exposure.
- `DEFAULT_AUTO_EXPOSURE` (const): const DEFAULT_AUTO_EXPOSURE: Readonly<Required<AutoExposureConfig>> — Default clamped auto-exposure. The range is deliberately asymmetric: a bright street is already readable after AgX's shoulder, while a lamp-lit interior is the case that crushes, so the meter may lift 1.3 stops but only darken 0.7 — an artist's exposure survives.
- `METERING_HIGHLIGHT_CEILING` (const): const METERING_HIGHLIGHT_CEILING: number — Pixels count toward metering up to this multiple of {@link WHITE_POINT}. A window or a sun disc sits far above it and would otherwise pull the whole frame down to a silhouette.
- `MID_GREY` (const): const MID_GREY: 0.18 — Linear scene luminance of an 18% grey card — the auto-exposure metering target.
- `WHITE_POINT` (const): const WHITE_POINT: 1 — Calibration of the output pipeline, in linear scene luminance (1.0 = a white-looking surface at exposure 1).
- `adaptExposure` (function): function adaptExposure(current: number, target: number, deltaSeconds: number, adaptationSeconds = DEFAULT_AUTO_EXPOSURE.adaptationSeconds): number — Frame-rate independent blend of `current` toward `target`, exponential in time so a hitch does not overshoot and a steady view settles. `deltaSeconds` may be 0..∞; a zero-length step keeps `current`.
- `exposureForKey` (function): function exposureForKey(keyLuminance: number, config: AutoExposureConfig = {}): number — Exposure that places a frame whose key luminance is `keyLuminance` on {@link MID_GREY}, bounded by the authored range. A dark interior asks for more than `max` and gets `max`; a blown-out exterior asks for less than `min` and gets `min`, so the frame never runs away at either end.
- `keyLuminanceFromSamples` (function): function keyLuminanceFromSamples(samples: ArrayLike<number>): number — Key luminance of a metered frame: the median of its samples, each clamped to {@link METERING_HIGHLIGHT_CEILING}. A median rather than a mean because a bright sky, a window or a lamp is a large minority of the frame: averaging those in drags an interior down to a silhouette, where the median still reports the room.

## @jgengine/core/render/environment

- `EnvironmentSource` (type): type EnvironmentSource = | { kind: "gradient"; sky: string; ground: string; sun?: string; intensity?: number } /** Equirectangular HDR or EXR environment map loaded from `url`. */ | { kind: "hdri"; url: string; rotation?: number; intensity?: number } /** Six faces of a cube environment map, in three… — A declarative source for image-based scene lighting.

## @jgengine/core/render/lightProbes

- `IrradianceBakeInput` (interface): interface IrradianceBakeInput — Everything a bake needs for one volume: where the grid sits, how much sky reaches it, and what fills the dark.
- `IrradianceBakeSettings` (interface): interface IrradianceBakeSettings — Authored bake inputs stored beside the samples so a volume can be re-baked without the editor.
- `IrradianceVolume` (interface): interface IrradianceVolume — One irradiance volume authored on a scene document.
- `PROBE_STRIDE` (const): const PROBE_STRIDE: number — Floats stored per probe: {@link SH_COEFFICIENTS} × RGB.
- `SH_COEFFICIENTS` (const): const SH_COEFFICIENTS: 9 — Baked irradiance volume: a grid of second-order (9-coefficient, RGB) spherical-harmonic probes over a box region, sampled at runtime for ambient lighting. It is the datum an interior has that a hemisphere light cannot: a room's fill is its own, not the sky's, and it varies across the space.
- `bakeIrradianceVolume` (function): function bakeIrradianceVolume(input: IrradianceBakeInput): IrradianceVolume — Bakes an irradiance volume from authored inputs: sky radiance where the region is open, an authored ceiling/floor fill where it is enclosed, plus inverse-square lamp radiance. Each probe projects its directional radiance into L2 SH, so ambient varies across the grid and keeps a lit side instead of flattening to one number.

## @jgengine/core/render/lightingBalance

- `DEFAULT_IBL_AMBIENT_SCALE` (const): const DEFAULT_IBL_AMBIENT_SCALE: 0.5 — Ambient multiplier applied under image-based light when `iblAmbientScale` is unset.
- `FALLBACK_KEY_LIGHT` (const): const FALLBACK_KEY_LIGHT: Readonly<DirectionalLightingConfig> — Soft key added when authored lighting has no directional light: high, off to one side, shadowless.
- `balanceLightingForIbl` (function): function balanceLightingForIbl(lighting: LightingConfig | undefined): LightingConfig | undefined — Rebalance authored lighting for a scene that also has image-based light: trim the flat ambient term by `iblAmbientScale` (default 0.5) and, when no directional light is authored, add {@link FALLBACK_KEY_LIGHT} tinted by the ambient colour so forms keep a lit and a shaded side. Returns the input unchanged when there is nothing to adjust.

## @jgengine/core/render/lookMood

- `LookMood` (type): type LookMood = MoodPreset | MoodConfig — A mood: a preset name, or a preset with token overrides.
- `MOOD_PRESETS` (const): const MOOD_PRESETS: readonly MoodPreset[] — Every mood preset name, for pickers and validating a mood read from a URL or file.
- `MoodConfig` (interface): interface MoodConfig — A mood preset plus the few tokens a game's art direction usually moves. Unset fields keep the preset's value.
- `MoodPreset` (type): type MoodPreset = "day" | "bright" | "golden" | "dusk" | "overcast" | "night" — Named lighting mood: one art-direction choice that sets the sun, the sky fill, the haze and the colour grade together, so they agree. `"day"` is a clear afternoon, `"bright"` a saturated high-fill cartoon day, `"golden"` a low warm late-afternoon sun with long shadows, `"dusk"` a sunset, `"overcast"` soft diffuse light under cloud, `"night"` moonlight.
- `MoodSun` (interface): interface MoodSun — Where the key light stands and how strong it is. Angles in degrees: azimuth 0 = -Z, 90 = +X; elevation 90 = overhead.
- `ResolvedMood` (interface): interface ResolvedMood — Concrete lighting, sky and grade a mood expands to.
- `resolveMood` (function): function resolveMood(mood: LookMood): ResolvedMood — Expand a mood into the lighting rig, sky and grade it stands for. The key light is the sun (the moon under `"night"`), casts cascaded shadows that follow the camera, and agrees with the dome's sun; a cool bounce opposite it keeps shadowed sides readable; the haze matches the horizon.

## @jgengine/core/render/lookPreset

- `CINEMATIC_POST_PROCESSING` (const): const CINEMATIC_POST_PROCESSING: PostProcessingConfig — Tuned tone-map + bloom + gentle SSAO + vignette/grade stack — the shipped-game post look. ACES, not the pipeline's AgX: under a sunny sky AgX's flat curve reads as a milky veil over the whole frame, and every shipped game had already switched this preset to ACES by hand.
- `CINEMATIC_SKY` (const): const CINEMATIC_SKY: SkyEnvironmentConfig — A static day sky: a real dome plus the shell's view-following shadow-casting sun and hemisphere fill.
- `COMIC_POST_PROCESSING` (const): const COMIC_POST_PROCESSING: PostProcessingConfig — Ink outlines, four cel bands and a punchy grade — a hand-inked comic look on any model.
- `GameLookInput` (interface): interface GameLookInput — Explicit graphics knobs a game may set; the preset only fills the ones left undefined.
- `LOOK_PRESETS` (const): const LOOK_PRESETS: readonly LookPreset[] — Every look preset name, for pickers and validating a preset read from a URL or file.
- `LookPreset` (type): type LookPreset = "neutral" | "photoreal" | "toon" | "comic" | "retro" | "cinematic" | "flat" — Named look preset composing the existing lighting/sky/fog/post knobs into one field. `"cinematic"` (the default when unset) draws a scene lit like a shipped game — a real day sky with a view-following shadow-casting sun + hemisphere fill, a network-free image-based-lighting environment so PBR surfaces catch soft reflections, and a tuned tone-map/bloom/AO/contact-shadow/vignette post stack, antialiased temporally on high and ultra. `"neutral"` keeps presentation unstyled. `"comic"` adds ink outlines and cel bands over a saturated grade (Borderlands-style); `"retro"` pixelates and posterizes the frame. `"flat"` opts out of the sky/IBL/post rig to the bare ambient+directional default (pre-#773). The upgraded default primitive materials — tuned roughness/metalness plus subtle procedural surface detail so un-modeled boxes/capsules stop reading as flat plastic — apply under both presets.
- `NEUTRAL_POST_PROCESSING` (const): const NEUTRAL_POST_PROCESSING: PostProcessingConfig — Unstyled baseline: no bloom or grade; contact AO stays at the graphics-tier default.
- `PHOTOREAL_POST_PROCESSING` (const): const PHOTOREAL_POST_PROCESSING: PostProcessingConfig — High-contrast physically based presentation for authored HDR environments.
- `RETRO_POST_PROCESSING` (const): const RETRO_POST_PROCESSING: PostProcessingConfig — Chunky pixels and posterized colour with no smoothing — a low-resolution retro look.
- `ResolvedGameLook` (interface): interface ResolvedGameLook — Concrete lighting/backdrop/post the shell renders after the preset has filled unset knobs.
- `TOON_POST_PROCESSING` (const): const TOON_POST_PROCESSING: PostProcessingConfig — Clean graphic presentation; toon materials remain game-owned while this sets the grade.
- `mergePostProcessing` (function): function mergePostProcessing(preset: PostProcessingConfig, authored: PostProcessingConfig | undefined): PostProcessingConfig — Deep-merge a game's partial post chain over a preset's. Every field the game set wins, including `false` to drop a stage; fields it left unset come from the preset, and stage objects merge field by field (tuples such as `grade.lift` replace whole).
- `resolveGameLook` (function): function resolveGameLook(input: GameLookInput): ResolvedGameLook — Expand a game's `look` and `mood` into concrete lighting/backdrop/post. The default look is `"cinematic"`; `"flat"` passes the explicit knobs through untouched.

## @jgengine/core/render/postProcessing

- `AoConfig` (interface): interface AoConfig — Ground-truth ambient occlusion stage — darkens contact creases and cavities for depth.
- `AtmosphereConfig` (interface): interface AtmosphereConfig — Air over the lit frame: ground haze that thickens toward the ground and with distance, brighter toward the sun, light shafts where the sky shows through gaps, and a glow around every nearby point and spot light as its light scatters in the same haze. Shafts need a shadow-casting sun. With no sun the whole pass is skipped unless `indoor` is set, which keeps the haze and the lamp glow running so a sunless interior gets its air and its lit lamps.
- `BloomConfig` (interface): interface BloomConfig — UnrealBloom stage — soft HDR glow around bright pixels (sun, glints, emissive).
- `ContactShadowConfig` (interface): interface ContactShadowConfig — Screen-space contact shadows: a short ray toward the sun from every pixel, against the depth buffer.
- `DEFAULT_AO` (const): const DEFAULT_AO: Readonly<AoConfig> — Contact shading used when a post chain leaves `ao` unset: soft creases, no dark halos.
- `DEFAULT_ATMOSPHERE` (const): const DEFAULT_ATMOSPHERE: Readonly<Required<AtmosphereConfig>> — Height haze and light shafts used when a post chain leaves `atmosphere` unset.
- `DEFAULT_CONTACT_SHADOWS` (const): const DEFAULT_CONTACT_SHADOWS: Readonly<Required<ContactShadowConfig>> — Contact shadows used when a post chain leaves `contactShadows` unset.
- `DofConfig` (interface): interface DofConfig — Depth-of-field (bokeh) stage — throws the fore/background out of focus around a focus distance.
- `GradeConfig` (interface): interface GradeConfig — Final colour-grade stage: lift/gain/gamma, saturation, vignette, film grain — applied in display space after tone mapping.
- `GradeLut` (type): type GradeLut = { url: string; size?: number } | { cube: LutCube } — A grade's LUT: a strip PNG (one `size`-wide tile per blue slice) or a baked cube.
- `LutCube` (interface): interface LutCube — A baked display-space LUT cube: `size³` RGB entries with red varying fastest, three bytes per entry in 0..255. Kept as plain data so a scene document can author one and a test can assert on it.
- `OutlineConfig` (interface): interface OutlineConfig — Ink outlines traced from depth and surface-normal edges — silhouettes plus interior creases.
- `PostAaMode` (type): type PostAaMode = "taa" | "smaa" | "msaa" | false — Edge antialiasing for the post chain. `"taa"` jitters the camera a fraction of a pixel each frame and blends the frames, which also settles shimmering foliage, thin wires and specular sparkle. SMAA runs in linear-sRGB before the output tone-map and cleans alpha-tested foliage/particles that MSAA samples alone leave crawling. `"msaa"` keeps only the render-target multisample resolve; `false` disables AA stages.
- `PostProcessingConfig` (interface): interface PostProcessingConfig — Declarative post-processing chain (RenderPass → AO → contact shadows → atmosphere → Bloom → DOF → SMAA or TAA → tone-map output → Grade). Present on a game means the shell mounts an `EffectComposer` and owns the render; absent means the renderer draws directly (unchanged). Each stage is a config object, `false` to skip, or omitted for its default. Pure data — no three.js types leak into core.
- `STUDIO_STAGE_POST` (const): const STUDIO_STAGE_POST: PostProcessingConfig — A cinematic "product shot" post preset — the full chain on (contact-AO, soft bloom, a warm film grade with vignette + a touch of grain + chromatic aberration). Meant for a `StudioStage` where a single parametric asset is framed on a backdrop, so every studio reads shipped, not intern-tier. DoF is left off by default (it needs a per-scene focus distance); set `dof` to enable it.
- `StylizeConfig` (interface): interface StylizeConfig — Art-style stage that turns the same models and lighting into a different look without touching materials: ink outlines (comic / Borderlands), cel bands (cartoon), pixelation (retro). Runs after tone mapping, before the grade.
- `ToneMappingMode` (type): type ToneMappingMode = "aces" | "agx" | "reinhard" | "cineon" | "linear" | "none" — Renderer tone-mapping curve applied by the post chain's output stage. `"agx"` is the pipeline default: it keeps hue in saturated highlights and rolls a sun-lit surface off gradually, where `"aces"` skews bright colours toward white.

## @jgengine/core/settings/frameRateLimit

- `FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_DISPLAY` (const): const FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_DISPLAY: "display" — Stored value for "render every display refresh" — the browser's vsync-locked rate.
- `FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS` (const): const FRAME_RATE_LIMIT_OPTIONS: readonly SettingOption[] — Frame-rate limit choices. Browsers always present on the display's vsync, so the uncapped option runs at the monitor's refresh rate; the numeric caps skip refreshes to save GPU and battery.

## @jgengine/core/settings/keybindingMenu.view

- `KeybindingMenu` (function): function KeybindingMenu({ session, theme, title = "Controls", resetAllLabel = "Reset All", capturePrompt = "Press a key…", onChange, className, style, }: KeybindingMenuProps): ReactNode — A drop-in controls-settings surface for a {@link RebindSession}: one row per action showing its label and current key glyph. Clicking a row arms capture ("Press a key…") and a window `keydown` listener feeds the pressed `event.code` to `session.capture`; rows that collide with another action show a conflict badge; each row has a Reset button and the panel has a Reset-all button. Presentation only — all conflict/capture/reset logic lives in the core session, and action ids/labels are the game's free strings. Reskin via {@link KeybindingMenuTheme} or ambient HudTheme tokens. A game owns its overall settings layout; this is the reusable controls block it drops in.

- `useRebindSession` (function): function useRebindSession(session: RebindSession): RebindSession — Subscribe to a rebind session and re-render on every change (capture, reset, arm/disarm, restore). Returns the session unchanged for convenient inline use.

A value of another primitive type converts when the result is the same value in the asked-for type (a number as its digits, a boolean as `"true"`/`"false"`); otherwise it throws {@link SettingsTypeError}, naming the key and both types, instead of handing back the fallback as if nothing were stored.

- `ActionCost` (interface): interface ActionCost — Headless view model for a contextual action collection — the data layer behind an RTS command card, an ability action bar, a build menu, or a radial. It carries *what the buttons mean* (label, hotkey, cost, cooldown, disabled reasons, toggle state) with zero rendering opinion, so a game keeps layout, dimensions, hotkeys, catalog-id mapping, renderer, and chrome caller-owned. The React renderers in `@jgengine/core/hud/actionHud.view` consume this; a game can swap either without forking the logic here.

Every field except `id` is optional so a build button, a stance toggle, and a cooldown ability all use the same shape. Catalog-id mapping (turning `icon`/`label` into art and copy) stays caller-owned.

- `LookPreset` (type): type LookPreset = "neutral" | "photoreal" | "toon" | "comic" | "retro" | "cinematic" | "flat" — Named look preset composing the existing lighting/sky/fog/post knobs into one field. `"cinematic"` (the default when unset) draws a scene lit like a shipped game — a real day sky with a view-following shadow-casting sun + hemisphere fill, a network-free image-based-lighting environment so PBR surfaces catch soft reflections, and a tuned tone-map/bloom/AO/contact-shadow/vignette post stack, antialiased temporally on high and ultra. `"neutral"` keeps presentation unstyled. `"comic"` adds ink outlines and cel bands over a saturated grade (Borderlands-style); `"retro"` pixelates and posterizes the frame. `"flat"` opts out of the sky/IBL/post rig to the bare ambient+directional default (pre-#773). The upgraded default primitive materials — tuned roughness/metalness plus subtle procedural surface detail so un-modeled boxes/capsules stop reading as flat plastic — apply under both presets.

Reduced motion collapses every duration to zero instead of skipping the state machine, so callers never branch on it.

It carries an ordered stack of opaque {@link ModalRecord}s (push to open, pop/resolve to close) and nothing about how they look: the model NEVER interprets a record's `kind` or a resolution's `result` string — those are free-form game vocabulary the React chrome in `@jgengine/react` renders. Observable ({@link ModalStack.subscribe}) and round-trips through a save ({@link ModalStack.snapshot}/{@link ModalStack.restore}). An injected clock powers optional per-modal auto-dismiss timers; leave those unset and the model is pure and clockless.

Delivered to the `onResolve` option and stashed as {@link ModalStack.lastResolution}.

- `ModalStackOptions` (interface): interface ModalStackOptions — Options for {@link createModalStack}.
- `ModalStackSnapshot` (interface): interface ModalStackSnapshot — Serializable state — the ordered entries (bottom-first) and the id counter. Plain JSON.

- `ObjectiveBannerController` (interface): interface ObjectiveBannerController — A live, clock-driven objective/stage banner controller.

This object is pooled and overwritten on the next {@link ObjectiveBannerController.current} call — read it, don't retain it.

It carries *which panels are open*, their focus/z stacking order, per-panel position overrides, and exclusive-group membership, with zero rendering opinion. The React chrome in `@jgengine/core/ui/panels.view` consumes this; a game keeps layout, skin, keybinds, and window content caller-owned. Pure and immutable: every reducer returns a new state and never mutates its input.

Plain JSON — persist and rehydrate it freely.

Present on a game means the shell mounts an `EffectComposer` and owns the render; absent means the renderer draws directly (unchanged). Each stage is a config object, `false` to skip, or omitted for its default. Pure data — no three.js types leak into core.

A partial `sweep` (e.g. `Math.PI` for a bottom half, `Math.PI / 2` for a quarter) packs the slices evenly inside `[startAngle, startAngle + sweep]` — the arc/quick-bar forms. Angles are radians from "up" (−Y), clockwise.

- `STUDIO_STAGE_POST` (const): const STUDIO_STAGE_POST: PostProcessingConfig — A cinematic "product shot" post preset — the full chain on (contact-AO, soft bloom, a warm film grade with vignette + a touch of grain + chromatic aberration). Meant for a `StudioStage` where a single parametric asset is framed on a backdrop, so every studio reads shipped, not intern-tier. DoF is left off by default (it needs a per-scene focus distance); set `dof` to enable it.

- `TEXT_SCALE_MIN` (const): const TEXT_SCALE_MIN: 0.75 — Minimum UI text scale.

Returns the first match's id, or null. Matching by hotkey does not consider `enabled`; the caller decides whether to fire a disabled action's feedback.

- `createAccessibilityStore` (function): function createAccessibilityStore(initial: Partial<AccessibilityState> = {}): AccessibilityStore — Serializable, observable store of accessibility preferences (reduced motion, high contrast, text scale, colorblind mode, captions). Genre-agnostic plumbing like input rebinding — a game binds these to its settings UI and adapts its presentation; `snapshot`/`restore` round-trip through a save or settings blob.
- `createCoachMarkSequence` (function): function createCoachMarkSequence(options: CoachMarkSequenceOptions): CoachMarkSequence — An onboarding coach-mark run: an ordered sequence of hint steps, each shown as a centered callout or anchored to a UI element, with a persisted "seen" set so completed onboarding stays done across sessions, and data-first condition gating so a step waits until its trigger id is satisfied. Advance/skip/dismiss drive it; `snapshot`/`restore` round-trip the seen set through a save. Purely a model — a React host renders `current()`.
- `createI18n` (function): function createI18n(options: I18nOptions): I18n — Create a translator over a message catalog: active-locale lookup with a fallback-locale chain, `{param}` interpolation, and `Intl.PluralRules`-based pluralization. Observable (`subscribe`) so React re-renders on `setLocale`; the catalog is caller-owned static data, the locale is the only state.
- `createMenuTransition` (function): function createMenuTransition(config: MenuTransitionConfig = {}, initial?: MenuTransitionSnapshot): MenuTransition — Create a {@link MenuTransition}. `open`/`close` start a phase; `tick` advances it once its duration has elapsed. Nothing schedules timers here — the caller ticks from its animation loop or a timeout.
- `createModalStack` (function): function createModalStack(options: ModalStackOptions = {}): ModalStack — A stack of modal dialogs: push opaque records to open blocking overlays (a pause menu, a confirm prompt, a reward popup), pop or resolve them with a free-form result to close, and query the top / open / depth to gate game input. The model is deliberately vocabulary-free — it never reads a record's `kind` or a resolution's `result`, so a game owns every dialog style — and fully serializable, with an optional injected clock driving per-modal auto-dismiss. A React host renders `top()`; `subscribe` re-renders it, `snapshot`/`restore` round-trip it through a save.
- `createObjectiveBanner` (function): function createObjectiveBanner(options: ObjectiveBannerOptions = {}): ObjectiveBannerController — A serializable, clock-driven stage/objective banner controller: the classic transient centered title stamp ("WAVE 3", "VICTORY", "OBJECTIVE COMPLETE"). A game calls `announce({ title, subtitle?, kind? })` and the controller queues it, flies it in, holds it, and fades it out on an injected clock — one banner at a time — exposing the current banner plus its phase (in/hold/out) and `progress` `0..1` for a renderer to animate opacity/scale/translate. Nothing here is genre-specific: `kind` is a free label the game owns and styles, and all timings are parameters. Call `advance()` each frame; `current()` returns the pooled view to draw; `snapshot`/`restore` round-trips the queue through a save.
- `createPanelState` (function): function createPanelState(defs: readonly PanelDef[]): PanelState — Build the initial {@link PanelState} from the panel defs: panels flagged `initial` start open (in declaration order, respecting group exclusivity), and every def's group/closable is captured into the state so later reducers need no defs.
- `createPhotoModeStore` (function): function createPhotoModeStore(initial: Partial<PhotoModeState> = {}): PhotoModeStore — Serializable, observable photo-mode state (active + hide-HUD). Genre-agnostic plumbing — a game engages it to free its camera and hide gameplay chrome for a clean capture, and reads `hideHud` to conditionally render its HUD. Pair with React `PhotoModeControls` and shell `captureCanvas`.
- `createSettingsStore` (function): function createSettingsStore(storage: Pick<WebStorageLike, "getItem" | "setItem"> | null | undefined = defaultStorage()): SettingsStore — Reactive, localStorage-backed settings store shared by the shell wiring and React hooks.
- `focusPanel` (function): function focusPanel(state: PanelState, id: string): PanelState — Raise open panel `id` to the top of the focus stack (assign it the highest z). No-op if it is closed or already on top, so a pointer-down that refocuses the top window returns the same state.
- `formatDelta` (function): function formatDelta(seconds: number, decimals: 0 | 1 | 2 = 2): string — Format a signed time gap as `+m:ss.ff` / `-m:ss.ff`, for race deltas and split times.
- `formatDistance` (function): function formatDistance(meters: number, options: DistanceFormat = {}): string — Format a distance given in meters as a HUD-ready string, switching to km automatically past 1000m when `unit: "auto"`.
- `formatDuration` (function): function formatDuration(seconds: number, options: DurationFormat = {}): string — Format a duration in seconds as a clock string (`m:ss`, `m:ss.ff`, or `h:mm:ss`), the shape every timer and racing HUD needs.
- `formatOrdinal` (function): function formatOrdinal(value: number): string — English ordinal for a placement number: 1 → "1st", 2 → "2nd", 3 → "3rd", 11 → "11th".
- `formatSpeed` (function): function formatSpeed(metersPerSecond: number, options: SpeedFormat = {}): string — Format a speed given in meters/second as a HUD-ready string in km/h, mph, knots, or m/s — the one conversion table every speedometer and telemetry readout should share.
- `hudScaleForViewport` (function): function hudScaleForViewport(fit: Required<HudFitConfig>, viewport: HudSize): number — The one scaling rule for every display: the ratio of the live viewport to the authored design size along the limiting axis, clamped. 1 on a viewport at or above design size; smoothly below 1 down to `minScale` on phones.
- `interpolate` (function): function interpolate(template: string, params?: TParams): string — Replace `{name}` placeholders in `template` with `params[name]`. Unknown placeholders are left intact. Pure and locale-independent.
- `isOpen` (function): function isOpen(state: PanelState, id: string): boolean — Whether panel `id` is currently open.
- `layoutScreenMarker` (function): function layoutScreenMarker(projection: ScreenProjection, viewport: ScreenMarkerViewport, options: ScreenMarkerOptions = {}): ScreenMarkerLayout — Pure, allocation-aware screen-marker math: given a projected target point, the viewport, and a `margin`, decide whether the target is on-screen and where to draw its marker. An on-screen point passes straight through (`onScreen: true`). An off-screen — or behind-camera — point is CLAMPED to the viewport edge (inset by `margin`) with `angle` set to the bearing from screen center toward the target, so a caller can pin an arrow to the frame edge and rotate it to point the way. Behind-camera projections have mirrored coordinates, so the bearing is flipped to face the true direction. This is the edge-clamp/arrow half that `layoutEntityFrames` lacks (it culls off-screen entries instead). No allocation when an `out` object is supplied — reuse one across a whole frame's waypoints.
- `listHudPanelTypes` (function): function listHudPanelTypes(): HudPanelTypeDef[] — Every registered panel type, sorted by id — editor palette / agent listing.
- `menuIntentForKey` (function): function menuIntentForKey(code: string): MenuIntent | null — Resolve a `KeyboardEvent.code` to a menu intent, or `null` for keys the menu leaves alone (typing, Tab, shortcuts). Escape and Backspace both mean back; Space and Enter both mean confirm.
- `menuIntentForPadAxis` (function): function menuIntentForPadAxis(axis: number, value: number, deadzone = 0.55): MenuNavDirection | null — Resolve a left-stick axis sample to a direction. Axis `0` is horizontal and axis `1` vertical (standard mapping, up is negative); the larger magnitude wins so a diagonal push is one move.
- `menuIntentForPadButton` (function): function menuIntentForPadButton(button: number): MenuIntent | null — Standard-mapping gamepad buttons as menu intents: A/Cross confirms, B/Circle and Start back, the d-pad moves. Buttons with no menu meaning return `null`.
- `menuNavIdAt` (function): function menuNavIdAt(ids: readonly string[], index: number): string | null — The id at `index`, or `null` outside the list.
- `menuNavIndex` (function): function menuNavIndex(ids: readonly string[], id: string | null | undefined): number — The index of `id` in the focus order, or `-1` when it is not part of this menu.
- `menuNavMove` (function): function menuNavMove(index: number, direction: MenuNavDirection, layout: MenuNavLayout): number — The next focused index for a direction, or the same index when the move is a no-op. Moves skip `disabled` indices and stop (rather than wrap) when every item in the way is disabled, so a menu can never hand focus to a dead row.
- `menuTransitionDurations` (function): function menuTransitionDurations(config: MenuTransitionConfig = {}): { enter: number; exit: number } — The enter and exit durations after reduced-motion is applied.
- `menuTransitionPhaseMs` (function): function menuTransitionPhaseMs(phase: MenuTransitionPhase, config: MenuTransitionConfig = {}): number — How long the current phase lasts, in ms (0 for open/closed).
- `moveGridFocus` (function): function moveGridFocus(current: number, count: number, columns: number, dir: FocusDirection, options?: GridFocusOptions): number — Pure grid focus math for keyboard and controller navigation of an action card laid out in `columns`-wide rows. Given the current index (`-1` for none) it returns the next index, clamped to `[0, count)` — or wrapped when `wrap` is set. `left/right` move within/across columns, `up/down` across rows, `next/prev` walk the flat order, `first/last` jump to the ends. Renderer-agnostic: radial and list layouts pass `columns: 1` (or `count`) to get sensible 1-D stepping.
- `movePanel` (function): function movePanel(state: PanelState, id: string, pos: PanelPosition): PanelState — Set panel `id`'s position override — the drag commit. Does not require the panel to be open, so a caller can pre-place a window before it is shown.
- `moveSelectionFocus` (function): function moveSelectionFocus(count: number, current: number, dir: SelectionFocusDirection): number — Pure next-focus math for the selection strip: step the focus index by one member (wrapping), or jump to an end. `-1` (no focus) steps to the first/last member. Returns `-1` for an empty selection.
- `openPanel` (function): function openPanel(state: PanelState, id: string): PanelState — Open panel `id`, raising it to the top of the focus stack. If it belongs to a `group`, the other open panels in that group are closed (exclusive windows). Opening an already-open panel just refocuses it. Position overrides are preserved.
- `orderedOpen` (function): function orderedOpen(state: PanelState, defs: readonly PanelDef[]): PanelDef[] — The open panels' defs sorted ascending by z — the render order for a window host (map to elements so the last, highest-z window paints on top). Defs unknown to the state are skipped.
- `orientationGateActive` (function): function orientationGateActive(requirement: OrientationRequirement, liveOrientation: LayoutOrientation): boolean — The rotate gate blocks gameplay: a hard requirement (or `unsupported`) the live orientation doesn't satisfy.
- `orientationHintActive` (function): function orientationHintActive(requirement: OrientationRequirement, liveOrientation: LayoutOrientation): boolean — An advisory rotate hint applies: a preference (not a hard gate) the live orientation doesn't satisfy.
- `overflowingPanels` (function): function overflowingPanels(panels: readonly { id: string; rect: HudRect }[], viewport: HudSize, tolerance = 1.5): HudOverflow[] — Every panel rect that escapes the viewport — the data behind the HUD overflow gate. A rect is only reported when it is partly visible *and* crosses an edge; a fully off-screen (closed/hidden) surface is skipped, so parked drawers and unopened menus never raise a false alarm.
- `panelByHotkey` (function): function panelByHotkey(defs: readonly PanelDef[], code: string): string | null — Find the panel whose `hotkey` matches `code`, case-insensitively — the keybind router. `code` may be a `KeyboardEvent.code` (`"KeyB"`) or key (`"b"`); it is compared verbatim to each def's `hotkey`, so author the hotkey in whichever form the caller feeds in. Returns the first match's id, or null.
- `placePopover` (function): function placePopover(anchor: UiRect, content: UiSize, viewport: UiSize, options?: PopoverOptions): PopoverPlacement — Position a popover/tooltip of `content` size against its `anchor` rectangle inside `viewport`: open on the `preferred` side, flip to the opposite when that side lacks room and the opposite has more, then clamp the top-left so the box stays fully on screen (respecting `margin`). Pure and deterministic — no DOM reads — so it is SSR-safe and unit-testable, and the React tooltip is a thin shell over it.
- `radialIndexFromAngle` (function): function radialIndexFromAngle(angle: number, count: number, arc?: RadialArc): number — Map an angle to a slice index; returns -1 when the angle falls outside a partial `arc`.
- `radialIndexFromVector` (function): function radialIndexFromVector(dx: number, dy: number, count: number, options: RadialVectorOptions = {}): number | null — Pick the slice a pointer/stick vector points at. `dx`/`dy` are screen-space (y down): up is `(0, -1)`. - `radialSlicePosition` (function): function radialSlicePosition(index: number, count: number, radius: number, arc?: RadialArc): { x: number; y: number } — Unit-circle position of a slice center (up = `(0, -1)`), scaled by `radius` — where to place a wedge's icon/label.
- `radialSlices` (function): function radialSlices(count: number, arc?: RadialArc): RadialSlice[] — Divide a ring (or `arc`) into `count` wedges — the geometry a radial/quick menu (weapon wheel, emote arc, ping bar) renders. A full wheel centers index 0 at the top; a partial `arc` packs the slices inside its sweep.
- `reducedMotionDuration` (function): function reducedMotionDuration(state: AccessibilityState, ms: number, reduced = 0): number — Return `ms` when motion is allowed, or `reduced` (default 0) when `reducedMotion` is set — the animation-duration gate.
- `registerHudPanelType` (function): function registerHudPanelType(def: HudPanelTypeDef): void — Register a HUD panel type so the editor can list/add/configure it and canvas resize knows axes.
- `resizePanelSize` (function): function resizePanelSize(current: HudSize, delta: { dw: number; dh: number }, axes: HudResizeAxes, limits?: { minWidth?: number; maxWidth?: number; minHeight?: number; maxHeight?: number; }): HudSize — Semantic resize: apply pixel deltas only on growable axes, clamped to min/max. Never scales content — callers reflow layout size (track length, list rows).
- `resolveAction` (function): function resolveAction(def: ActionDef): ResolvedAction — Resolve one {@link ActionDef} into a {@link ResolvedAction}: normalize label, compute `enabled`, and order the blocking `reasons`. Pure — the same input always yields the same view model.
- `resolveActionCollection` (function): function resolveActionCollection(defs: readonly ActionDef[]): ResolvedAction[] — Resolve an ordered list of actions, preserving input order.
- `resolveGameLook` (function): function resolveGameLook(input: GameLookInput): ResolvedGameLook — Expand a game's `look` and `mood` into concrete lighting/backdrop/post. The default look is `"cinematic"`; `"flat"` passes the explicit knobs through untouched.
- `resolveHudFit` (function): function resolveHudFit(config: HudViewportConfig | undefined, mobile: boolean): Required<HudFitConfig> — ⚠ undocumented
- `resolveHudPanelLayout` (function): function resolveHudPanelLayout(docPanel: EditorUiPanelLayout | undefined, fallback: HudPanelFallback): ResolvedHudPanelLayout — Resolve a panel's layout: document entry wins field-by-field over TSX fallback. TSX props are fallback-only — the scene document is the source of truth once authored.
- `resolveOrientationRequirement` (function): function resolveOrientationRequirement(orientation: GameOrientation | undefined, platform: "mobile" | "desktop"): OrientationRequirement — Resolve the game's orientation declaration into a concrete requirement for a platform. Desktop is always unconstrained.
- `selectionWindow` (function): function selectionWindow(members: readonly EntitySummaryDef[], scroll: number, size: number): SelectionWindow — Compute a virtualization window over a large selection: a `size`-length slice starting near `scroll`, clamped so the window never runs past the end. Render only `items`, offsetting by `start * itemSize`, to keep a thousand-unit selection from mounting a thousand portraits.
- `shouldRepeatMenuNav` (function): function shouldRepeatMenuNav(now: number, hold: MenuNavHold, repeat: MenuNavRepeat = {}): boolean — Whether a held direction should fire a move at `now`: immediately on press, then only after `delayMs`, and no more often than `intervalMs`. Pure timing, so a gamepad poll and a keydown handler share one rule.
- `summarizeSelection` (function): function summarizeSelection(members: readonly EntitySummaryDef[], options?: SummarizeSelectionOptions): SelectionView — Summarize a selected-entity list into a {@link SelectionView}: resolve the primary focus, keep the ordered members, and bucket them by `kind`.
